svg.title: How the apply job decides whether a text of the answer holds a secret
svg.desc: A known kind of token refuses the answer wherever it is. Any other text is looked at in runs of 40 or more letters, digits and the characters plus, slash, equals sign, underscore and dash, after the owner, the repository and the commit or branch of every link to GitHub are left out, unless the name of the repository or the branch has 32 or more characters, and every digest that names its algorithm, such as sha256:, is left out too. A run with lower case, upper case and digits is a key when it has the plus or equals sign of Base64 or its letters read like noise. Every other run is a key when it holds 64 or more characters of hex, or 40 or more of one case and digits with a letter beyond those of hex. A key is harmless when it is part of the path of a file that git tracks. Any other run is harmless.
